neighbors.establishing_passage: DeepISLES is the public ISLES'22 ensemble and was validated on ischemic-lesion segmentation; the paper does not audit imprint in ISLES'24 labels.
PADL models annotator preference and stochastic annotation error in medical segmentation.
The work learns and conditions on annotation styles across medical segmentation datasets.
A public hierarchical arterial-territory atlas was built from 1,298 acute-stroke lesion maps.
DeepISLES predictions were mapped to a reference atlas to evaluate affected vascular territory.
A native-CTP deep network predicts final infarct and uses treatment/time metadata.
The model learns final infarct directly from native CTP rather than deconvolved maps.
Temporal feature extractors learn tissue outcome from source concentration-time and residue curves.
In 1,843 cases, bolus peak timing correlated with age, ejection fraction, and scan triggering.
AI-derived 3D conjugate gaze correlated with NIHSS and hemispheric ischemia.
Visual CT eye deviation predicted ischemic-stroke diagnosis and NIHSS gaze score.
An NCCT ELVO system explicitly detected crystalline-lens deviation and included it in its learned decision pipeline.
A roughly 12,000-subject CT study measured age-related prevalence across physiologic intracranial calcification sites.
The study measures prevalence, location, and morphology of physiologic intracranial calcifications.
Pineal, choroid-plexus, and dural calcifications were quantified and positively associated with age in children.
Wavelet-Wiener residuals were used to identify individual CT scanners from sensor noise.
Sensor pattern noise and reconstruction footprints identify 15 scanner models from four manufacturers.
Head-CT CNNs distinguish scanner manufacturer, and acquisition bias changes classification and segmentation performance.
Detector width limits CTP coverage to roughly 4–16 cm, and limited coverage can miss ischemic extent.
Reduced CTP coverage underestimates ischemic lesion volume relative to whole-brain coverage.
The study estimates the z-axis coverage required to characterize MCA-territory perfusion abnormalities.
Day-5 MRI lesion volume overestimated day-90 infarct volume by 24%; CSF displacement was used to estimate edema.
Linear and nonlinear registrations were compared while quantifying edema-related anatomical distortion and infarct growth.
Cost-function masking was introduced to prevent focal lesions from biasing spatial normalization.
